description: Demolition of existing garage and construction of a 2-storey dwellinghouse at side with habitable basement.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location Plan 30/2503/001 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25Existing Block Site Plan 30/2503/002 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Existing Plans 30/2503/003 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Existing Front and Rear Elevations 30/2503/004 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Existing Side and Section AA 30/2503/005 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Demolition Plan 30/2503/006 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Proposed Block Site Plan 30/2503/007 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Proposed Detailed Site Plan 30/2503/008 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Proposed Plans 30/2503/009 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Proposed Elevations 1 30/2503/010 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Proposed Elevations 2 30/2503/011 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Proposed Section AA 30/2503/012 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Proposed Fire Escape Routes 30/2503/013 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Proposed Bin and Cycle Storages 30/2503/014 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Proposed Plans Inclusive Design for Part M 30/2503/015 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Detailed Drawing for Permeable Paving 30/2503/016 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Existing and Proposed Streetscene Drawing 30/2503/017 June 2025 RevA 26.06.25;Indicative Surface Water and Foul Drainage Strategy 25040-FCE-XX-XX-DR-D-0500 March 2025 Rev P01 31.03.25Accessibility Statement June 2025Provisional Structural Impact AssessmentEnergy StatementFire Statement June 2025Flood Risk Assessment and Sustainable Drainage Strategy June 2025Planning and Design & Access Statement June 2025Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) Statement March 2025Basement Impact Assessment (BIA) 21.04.25Construction Environmental Management Plan June 2025Daylight and Sunlight Assessment Report June 2025Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

No commencement of construction works shall take place until samples of all external facing materials have been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. The relevant works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved sample details. The following details are required:a)	External materials specification, samples and detailed drawings (at 1:20 and 1:5) including: brickwork detailing including bond, joint and mortar); soldier course and lintels, light fixtures;b)	Key roof junctions including green roof, parapets; balustrades or railings; window, rooflight and door openings and installations including frame material and dimensions (minimum reveal depth 1 brick / 215mm).c)	A landscaping scheme to include specification, layout plan, detail sections (1:5) including hard and soft landscaping, planting species, steps, retaining walls, tree details, boundary treatment, d)	Integration and screening of renewable technologies specified in the approved Energy Statement.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

Prior to commencement (Notwithstanding demolition and clearance of the site) of any construction work hereby permitted, a groundwater flood risk assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the following:o An onsite geological investigation;o Depth to groundwater and relative depth of the basement level;o Identification of groundwater flow routes, and demonstration that the proposed basement will not impact these   measures to reduce the impact of the basement on groundwater flows and flooding.REASON: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value.

Following practical completion of works a final Energy Performance Certificate with accompanying Building Regulations compliance report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where applicable, a Display Energy Certificate shall be submitted within 18 months following first occupation. Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

Prior to above ground works, a detailed 'Energy Report' shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Submitted details will demonstrate the energy efficiency of the development and shall provide for no less than a 35% improvement in total CO2 (carbon) emissions arising from the operation of the development and its services over Part L of Building Regs 2013.  The development shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the details so approved and maintained as such thereafter.REASON:  In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that carbon emission reduction targets are met in accordance with the Local Development Plan, the London Plan and the NPPF.

The residential unit hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the Building Regulations Optional requirement G2 for water consumption of no more than 105 litres or less per head per day (excluding allowance of up to five litres for external water consumption) has been complied with. The measures shall thereafter be permanently retained.Reason: To promote water conservation and efficiency measures in all new developments and where possible in the retrofitting of existing stock in accordance with Policy SI 5 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy CP21 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010).

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site have been provided within the development, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities to be retained permanently thereafter.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of the occupiers of adjoining premises; protect the general environment; prevent any obstruction to pedestrian movement and to ensure that there are adequate facilities for the storage and recycling of recoverable materials.

The dwelling hereby approved shall not be occupied until space has been laid out within the site [in accordance with drawing ref: Proposed Detailed Site Plan 30/2503/008 RevA] for:o The provision of 2 long stay cycle parking spaces in an accessible location. The access route to the store should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike to enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gate (excluding the store door).o Secured with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob   o Fully enclosed by 4 walls and a roofo Ability to lock a bicycle to a permanent fixture (e.g. Sheffield stand or wall anchor) The approved details shall thereafter be installed and permanently retained for cycle parking.Reason: To encourage sustainable means of transport, to provide secure cycle storage facilities free from obstruction, and in the interest of visual amenity.

Notwithstanding the provisions of classes A, B, C, D, E and F of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (or any amending Order), no enlargement, improvement, alteration, buildings, extensions or enclosure to the existing and new buildings hereby approved shall be carried out or erected without the prior approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and ensure that the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and to prevent the overdevelopment of the site.
No structure or obstruction higher than 0.6m should be within 2m from either side of any vehicle access point.  Reason:  To minimise danger, obstruction and inconvenience to users of the highway.
